concepts.title: Final Position on a Number Line
concepts.definition: If the first strike moves the coin 'a' units and the second strike moves the coin 'b' units, then the final position P is the sum of the two movements.
concepts.key_idea: The final position of an object moving in two steps is the algebraic sum of its individual displacements.

concepts.title: Additive Inverse
concepts.definition: Additive inverse of an integer a is represented as -a. The sum of an integer and its additive inverse is zero.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting a numberput differently,  is the same as adding its additive inverse.

concepts.title: Multiplication of Integers
concepts.definition: When two integers are multiplied, the product is positive if both have the same sign, and negative if they have different signs.
concepts.key_idea: The magnitude of the product is the product of magnitudes; the sign is positive for like signs and negative for unlike signs.

concepts.title: Commutative Property of Multiplication
concepts.definition: Multiplication is commutative for integers; the product does not change when the multiplier and multiplicand are swapped.
concepts.key_idea: The order of factors in multiplication does not affect the product.

concepts.title: Multiplication by -1
concepts.definition: The product of any integer a and -1 is the additive inverse of a.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying by -1 flips the sign of the integer.

concepts.title: Distributive Property
concepts.definition: Integer multiplication isin short,  distributive over addition.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying a sum by a number is the same as multiplying each addend by the number and then adding the products.

concepts.title: Division of Integers
concepts.definition: For any two positive integers a and b, a / (-b) = -(a / b), (-a) / b = -(a / b), and (-a) / (-b) = a / b.
concepts.key_idea: The sign rules for division are identical to the sign rules for multiplication.

concepts.title: Brahmagupta's Rules
concepts.definition: The product orsimply put,  quotient of two fortunes is a fortune. The product or quotient of two debts is a fortune. The product or quotient of a debt and a fortune is a debt.
concepts.key_idea: Historical rules for integer operations using 'fortune' for positive and 'debt' for negative.
